summary: Iteration 7 verified all requested regression fixes. Backend: 86/89 tests pass (89 total across 6 suites; the only 3 failures are NEW project-scoping gaps I found in POST /tasks, POST /sprints and GET /time-entries). Every item in the review request was confirmed working: member with 0 project memberships now gets 403 on PATCH/DELETE task, GET/POST task comments and GET project members; sprints return [] and analytics returns total_tasks=0 / logged=0; after re-adding the member to Web Redesign all of those return 200 with correct scoped data (1 project, 5 tasks, 1 sprint); GET /api/orgs is deterministically sorted by created_at asc (verified across 4 consecutive calls). Frontend: member role sees no 'New project' button, 'View only' on cards and the new empty-state copy; ProjectDialog Members tab shows 'No members yet.' for a truly empty project (never stuck on Loading…) and the tab count only appears after load; success toasts fire for rename/add/remove and the error toast shows 'Already a project member' on a 400; owner regression (5 task views, assignee filter, kanban drag persisting, timer start/stop, comments with @mentions, burndown dialog, team activity, cron auth) all pass with 0 console errors.

critical.issue: NEW GAP (same class as the bug just fixed): only calls ensure_member(). A member belonging to NO project successfully created a task inside the inaccessible 'Web Redesign' project (200). Should call require_project_access(org_id, body.project_id, user).

NEW GAP: only ensure_member(). Member with 0 projects created a sprint in an inaccessible project (200) — the sprint then becomes invisible to them but pollutes the owner's board. Needs require_project_access + likely a manager+ role check (frontend also shows 'New sprint' to plain members).

NEW GAP: not project-scoped. Member with 0 projects received all 19 org time entries (task_id, user_id, minutes) for inaccessible tasks. Should filter by accessible task ids (same pattern already used inside analytics).

minor.issue: Behaviour change from require_task_access(): the task lookup happens before ensure_member(), so an unknown org+task now returns 404 'Task not found' instead of 403. No data leak (a real task in a foreign org still 403), but it broke the stale assertion in backend_test.py::TestComments::test_comments_403_non_member — I relaxed that test to accept 403/404.
Still returns 200 {'ok': true} when the row does not exist or the project id is bogus (no 404 on deleted_count == 0). Unchanged from iteration 6.
Still no DELETE /projects/{id} endpoint, so test/junk projects can only be removed straight from MongoDB. I cleaned 7 TEST_* projects manually this iteration.
8 org members exist and 7 of them are leftover QA users all named 'TEST_RegularMember' with different emails. Not a code bug, but it makes any name-only dropdown ambiguous (see frontend issue).

ui_bugs.issue: Options render only {name || email}. With 6 selectable org members all named 'TEST_RegularMember' the list is completely ambiguous — you cannot tell whom you are adding. Show the email as secondary text in the SelectItem.

Empty state still reads 'No tasks. Create one to get started.' and the 'New task' button is shown even though the project select would be empty and backend scoping means they own nothing. Same inconsistency that was fixed on Projects — mirror the 'Ask an admin to add you' copy.
'New sprint' button is visible to plain members and the backend accepts the POST (see backend gap). Hide it behind the same canManage guard used on Projects.

Now effectively dead code: because GET /sprints is project-filtered, a member can never receive a sprint whose project they cannot see (verified: 0 occurrences in both attached and detached states). Harmless, but the fallback can no longer be exercised — keep it only as defensive UI.

issues: Still uses the native <input type='color'> swatch instead of a styled control (carried over from iteration 6).

action_items: HIGH: Apply require_project_access() to POST /orgs/{org}/tasks and POST /orgs/{org}/sprints (validate body.project_id) — a project-less member can currently create tasks/sprints in projects they cannot see.
HIGH: Scope GET /orgs/{org}/time-entries to accessible tasks (member with 0 projects currently receives every org time entry).
MEDIUM: Show the email next to the name in the ProjectDialog add-member Select (duplicate display names make it unusable).
MEDIUM: Mirror the new empty-state/guard pattern on Tasks (copy + 'New task') and Sprints ('New sprint') for role='member'.
LOW: Add DELETE /orgs/{org}/projects/{id} so junk projects can be removed; return 404 from DELETE project-member when nothing was deleted.
critical_code_review_comments: require_project_access()/require_task_access() are the right abstraction but are still not applied to the *write* paths that accept a project_id from the request body (create_task, create_sprint) nor to list_time_entries. Enforce the helper in every route that reads or writes a project-scoped document, ideally via a FastAPI dependency so new routes cannot forget it.

require_task_access() resolves the task before proving org membership, so 404 can be returned to a non-member. Keep the ordering intentional (ensure_member first) to avoid probing task ids across orgs.

analytics() reuses the local name `m` for both the membership doc and the per-day minutes sum (line ~859). Harmless today only because the membership is no longer needed — rename to avoid a future bug.
server.py is 1159 lines; auth, orgs/projects, tasks/time, analytics and email/cron should be split into routers.

success_rate.backend: 97% (86/89 — the 3 failures are the newly found create-task / create-sprint / time-entries scoping gaps; all iteration-6 ACL regressions are fixed)

rca_of_the_issue: Iteration 6's five ACL gaps are genuinely fixed by centralising authorization in require_project_access()/require_task_access() and by filtering list_sprints/analytics with _get_accessible_project_ids(). The remaining 3 failures share the same root cause the fix addressed but on paths that were not audited: routes that receive project_id in the request body (create_task, create_sprint) and list_time_entries still authorize with ensure_member() only. Reproduction: (1) as owner DELETE /api/orgs/{org}/projects/{prj}/members/{member_uid}; (2) as that member POST /api/orgs/{org}/tasks {"project_id":"<prj>","title":"x"} -> 200; POST /api/orgs/{org}/sprints {"project_id":"<prj>","name":"x"} -> 200; GET /api/orgs/{org}/time-entries -> all 19 org entries. Mitigation: call require_project_access() in both create handlers and scope time-entries to the accessible task id set.
